summary: Talents own talent/tree identity (TalentTreeDB, TalentRegistry, canonical UUID helpers), prerequisite data, eight active talent action modules and the custom talent tree workbench. Identity and membership are well tested; the action layer holds the largest A-02 concentration (72 direct writes in 11 files, none an exception), writes to other actors without a GM relay, reads the combatTurn hook arguments three different ways, mutates during render and in preUpdateActor, patches progression and GM-shell classes at runtime, and maintains a parallel bonus Force Point pool in a different flag scope from the one ActorEngine debits. No Foundry acceptance exists.

findings.title: 72 direct actor/owned-item writes across 11 live talent files (all violations)
findings.observed: Per-file classification (all violations of A-02; no exception comment, no world document): sith 25 = 12 own usage/state flags (encounterUses, rapidAlchemy, channelAnger, stolenForm, wildSense), 7 flags on target actors, 6 unsets in lifecycle hooks; consular 12 = 9 own encounter/turn flags + 3 on ally/target actors; force-adept 8 = owned Force power item.update (284), 2 owned weapon flags (511, 529), 1 target flag, 4 own flags; lightsaber 7 = Block/Deflect/Redirect/Riposte own state; sentinel 5 = own state; guardian-spirit 4 = bonus FP pool (91, see F-TAL-007) + 3 usage flags; lightsaber-form-engine 4 = active form/reaction state; jedi-prestige 3 = own flags + prior actor in hook; armor 1 = Shield Expert state; effect wizard 2 = item flags during render (F-TAL-005); approval service 1 = owned talent item.update by GM. Most actions also make a separate ActorEngine call for the cost, so state and cost are two writes.
findings.intendedOwnership: ActorEngine (updateActor with flags paths; updateOwnedItems for owned items), one write per action.
findings.proposedSolution: Introduce a talent-state helper over ActorEngine.updateActor (flags.foundryvtt-swse.talentState.<key>) and migrate file by file starting with sith/consular; fold the paired cost and state into one ActorEngine update; replace power.update/weapon.setFlag/item.update with ActorEngine.updateOwnedItems.
findings.alternatives: ActorEngine.setActorFlag/unsetActorFlag thin wrappers (keeps call shape, still single gate).
dependencies: F-TAL-002 (cross-actor writes need a relay first)
findings.regressionTests: Static guard: no setFlag/unsetFlag/update on actor or owned items in scripts/engine/talent/** except via ActorEngine; extend force-v2-03b-talent-contracts to assert one ActorEngine call per action.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Representative talent from each module used by a player-owned character.
findings.risk: Large surface; flag path changes need a migration or dual-read

findings.title: Cross-actor flag writes from the acting client without a GM relay
findings.observed: Flags are set on target/ally actors (pendingAfflictions, bondedMount, cripplingStrike, sithCommander.*, Adept Negotiator, pendingMasterAdvisorForcePoint, unsettlingPresence) directly from the client that runs the action. No socket, executeAsGM or GM relay exists in any talent action file. A player normally lacks update permission on enemy actors, so these writes are expected to fail for players; not run in Foundry.
findings.intendedOwnership: ActorEngine with a GM-authoritative relay for documents the user does not own.
findings.proposedSolution: Route cross-actor effects through a GM relay (existing project socket/GM-operation service if present, else a new ActorEngine.requestGmMutation) and store effects as ActiveEffects or target-owned records written by the GM.
findings.alternatives: Store the effect on the source actor and resolve it on the target at read time.
findings.regressionTests: Shim test with a non-owner user asserting the relay is used.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Player uses Affliction / Crippling Strike on a GM-owned NPC.

findings.title: combatTurn arguments read three different ways; Master Advisor reads a field the hook does not carry
findings.observed: The project's own combat hooks treat combatTurn as (combat, updateData, updateOptions). Sith reads combat.combatant; jedi-prestige reads arg2.combatant / arg2.actor (updateData has only round/turn, so priorActor is always null and the Master Advisor pending Force Point is never delivered); lightsaber reads arg3.combatant then falls back to combat.combatant. Whether combat.combatant is the ending or starting combatant at hook time determines whether Affliction damage and Block/Deflect resets hit the right actor; that depends on Foundry v13 call timing and is not verified. The listeners are also not gated to one client.
findings.intendedOwnership: One combat-turn event service (combat domain) that emits {combat, previousCombatant, currentCombatant} once on the responsible GM.
findings.proposedSolution: Subscribe talent lifecycle to a normalized swse turn event (or the existing updateCombat + isResponsibleGm pattern used by scripts/infrastructure/hooks/force-power-hooks.js:135) and use combat.previous / combat.combatant explicitly.
findings.regressionTests: Shim test driving a turn change asserting prior/current resolution for all three listeners.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Advance turns with Affliction pending and Master Advisor pending.

findings.title: Ungated deleteCombat cleanup and writes inside preUpdateActor
findings.observed: deleteCombat runs on every client; each loops combatants and issues unsetFlag/updateActor (non-owners error, caught for the whole loop). preUpdateActor awaits unsetFlag and a chat post while another update is in flight (Foundry does not await pre-hooks).
findings.intendedOwnership: Responsible-GM lifecycle service; no writes in pre-hooks.
findings.proposedSolution: Gate on isResponsibleGm(); move Crippling Strike cleanup to updateActor (post) with the same gate.
findings.regressionTests: Shim test: two users, one cleanup write.
findings.foundryAcceptance: End combat with two clients connected.

findings.title: Effect-wizard _onRender patch writes item flags during render
findings.observed: SWSEItemSheet.prototype._onRender is replaced; the replacement calls maybeAutoOpenCustomTalentWizard, which marks the auto-open consumed with item.unsetFlag/setFlag; a flag write on an owned item triggers another sheet render.
findings.intendedOwnership: UI-only state (wizard presented) in session/client memory, not document flags (OSI performance rule).
findings.proposedSolution: Keep "presented" in a client-side WeakSet/session map; consume the request flag via ActorEngine outside render (on wizard close).
findings.regressionTests: Static guard against document writes inside _onRender/_prepareContext.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Open a workbench-created talent sheet; one render, wizard opens once.

findings.title: Runtime monkey-patches of progression and GM-shell classes from the workbench
findings.observed: Four TalentStep.prototype methods, SWSEItemSheet.prototype._onRender, four GM approval service statics and GMDatapad.prototype._getHomeBadgeCounts are wrapped at index.js:252-254. Legacy class A (live, active) violating A-09 and the progression-architecture "no runtime patching" rule.
findings.intendedOwnership: Progression exposes a tree-provider registry; GM approvals expose a request-source registry; item sheet exposes a panel extension point.
findings.proposedSolution: Add the three extension points in their owning domains and convert each wrapper to a registration; delete the patches.
findings.regressionTests: Workbench overlay test asserting custom trees appear via the provider API.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Chargen with a custom tree; GM approval of custom content.
findings.risk: Medium; workbench has no behavioural tests

findings.title: Guardian Spirit bonus FP pool in a different flag scope than the pool ActorEngine debits
findings.observed: GuardianSpiritActions writes actor.setFlag('swse','bonusForcePoints'), which SWSEActorBase.setFlag redirects to flags['foundryvtt-swse']. Every other writer (ActorEngine.spendForcePoints debit, Force Flow, force-adept, jedi-prestige, feats) writes the literal path flags.swse.bonusForcePoints. getFlag('swse') returns the foundryvtt-swse value first. After any Guardian Spirit claim or manual sheet adjustment, reads return the foundryvtt-swse pool: ActorEngine debits are written to flags.swse and never seen again (bonus points re-spendable) and later grants from other sources are hidden. spendBonusForcePoints also debits without a V2 receipt, queue or round-limit check. No test covers guardian-spirit-actions.js.
findings.intendedOwnership: FRC: one bonus-pool API in ActorEngine/ForcePointsService (grant, expire, spend via spendForcePoints), one storage path.
findings.proposedSolution: Route GuardianSpirit grant/adjust through a single ActorEngine bonus-pool grant API writing the same path as spendForcePoints; route negative manual adjustment through an explicit MANUAL_ADJUSTMENT path; add a migration that merges any flags[foundryvtt-swse].bonusForcePoints into the canonical path. Extend the direct-FP-writer guard to the bonus pool.
findings.alternatives: Change all writers to setFlag('swse') consistently (still leaves the spend bypass).
findings.regressionTests: Shim test: claim Guardian Spirit, spend via ActorEngine.spendForcePoints, assert pool decremented and getFlag returns the decremented pool.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Guardian Spirit claim then FP spend, reload, check pool and ledger.
findings.risk: Existing worlds may already hold two copies; needs migration

findings.title: 11 engine->UI imports in talent action modules
findings.observed: Nine modules import SwseDialogV2 and two import the Force Alchemy workbench app; lightsaber exposes LIGHTSABER_TALENT_IO as a seam already.
findings.intendedOwnership: Engine receives choices through an injected prompt port (as LIGHTSABER_TALENT_IO does).
findings.proposedSolution: Generalize the LIGHTSABER_TALENT_IO pattern into a talent prompt port registered by the UI layer.

findings.title: Tree membership is an additive 3-source union owned by a progression-path module
findings.observed: Membership merges talent-side fields, a generated registry and tree claims (documented additive hydration). Correct for robustness but there is no declared single source, and disagreements are merged rather than reported. Three tree-related modules (membership authority, tree-authority, TalentTreeRegistry) live under progression.
findings.intendedOwnership: Talents domain declares membership derived from canonical talents.json treeId; others are hints with a drift report.
findings.proposedSolution: Declare owner in this contract, add a drift report test listing members contributed by only one source.

findings.title: Unreachable legacy talent-effects cluster
findings.observed: talents.js (TALENT_EFFECTS, 1,499 SLOC) and TalentNormalizerEngine are imported only by talent-effects-hooks.js, which has no importer; no pack/template reference found; listed in validate-mutation-sovereignty.js as a known file. Legacy class C candidate (talent-relationship-registry: static proof no runtime path).
findings.intendedOwnership: Feat/talent effect generation via FeatEffectApplier-style lifecycle if ever needed.
findings.proposedSolution: Owner confirms; delete the cluster and the sovereignty list entry.
findings.alternatives: Wire talent-effects-hooks if TALENT_EFFECTS is still intended (UNIMPLEMENTED integration).

findings.title: Local Dark Side Score increment helpers in force-adept and sith actions
findings.observed: Each computes DSPEngine.getNextValue and writes system.darkSide.value plus a differently shaped dspLog entry via ActorEngine.updateActor. DSPEngine has no mutation API. See F-FRC-004 for the full writer set.
findings.intendedOwnership: FRC Dark Side Score mutation API.
findings.proposedSolution: Use the FRC DSS API proposed in F-FRC-004.
